text: Each conversion call starts with a 100-byte output allowance, rejects a reported output length outside 0–100 and rejects consumed input at or below zero before append and pointer advance. Finish output has the same length guard. Converter return statuses and consumed <= remaining input are not explicitly checked. Failure may leave earlier valid chunks in the destination. The round-trip caller ignores the nsresult and compares strings. These are precise source limits, not a complete converter-safety or crash-cure claim; no failure injection or native run occurred.
title: Modified UTF-7 conversion validates reported output and positive input progress
